items.title: Johnny Varro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: It was just one big party with all the June Taylor dancers and Art Carney and Frank Fontaine and all that whole bunch, Sheila McRae.

ctx.x: Well when I was at Nick’s with Phil Napoleon in ’54, a lot of celebrities used to come in, people would come in and dig the music and stay until, God we went until four o’clock in the morning in those days. And we’d have an audience on for that last set, we’d have at least two dozen people there sitting around the bar waiting. I guess they had to go to work in the morning but the music was entrancing to them. And this one night Jackie came in with an entourage and sat and listened to the and loved the band. Phil…

hour variety show. And I got a call from Phil Napoleon again and he says, “What are you doing at this point?” I said, “Nothing.” He says, “Come on down, I’ve got the Gleason show, I’ve got the race track on Saturdays, and we’ve got a steady gig in the Roney Plaza Hotel six nights a week.” I said, “Send me a ticket.” And it was snowing, it was January, it was snowing in New York and horrible and freezing and I had no work. He says, “The temperature here is 78 degrees.” “Send me a ticket. I’ll be right down.” And I…
Oh, Frank Fontaine, I haven’t heard that name in a while. He was a great drunk, wasn’t he?
